what_it_is: Manastu Space is an IIT Bombay-linked space propulsion startup developing green (non-hydrazine) satellite propulsion, including its iBooster thruster line and MS-289 fuel formulation. The company tested its green propulsion system in space at the end of 2024 and has positioned itself around safer, higher-performance chemical propulsion for small satellites, plus space-safety technology.
india_angle: Manastu delivered an iBooster green propulsion system to DRDO under Technology Development Fund support, and publicly test-fired its system in space on 31 December 2024 - among the first private Indian in-space green-propulsion demonstrations. It raised a reported $3M pre-Series A in 2023 with follow-on funding in 2025 to scale commercial deployment.
intelligence_assessment: The DRDO TDF delivery and in-space firing give Manastu unusually concrete government-linked evidence for a private propulsion startup. Thrust-class performance, unit economics and customer ramp beyond government demos remain vendor-stated; watch repeat flight units and commercial satellite contracts as confirmation.

faq.a: Green satellite propulsion - the iBooster thruster family and MS-289 fuel - plus space-safety technology.

faq.q: Did Manastu test its propulsion in space?
faq.a: Yes - it publicly reported an in-space test firing of its green propulsion system on 31 December 2024.
It has publicly delivered an iBooster system to DRDO under Technology Development Fund (TDF) support.
